title: structured-output: add constrained-decoding backends (CFG / regex / tokenizer edge cases)
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: customers require robust structured-output guarantees (CFG/grammar, regex constraints) when using the Redwood API and the OpenAI-compatible layer. Current implementation mixes constraint logic into the single decoder loop which complicates streaming, makes tokenizer boundary handling fragile, and prevents easily swapping constraint engines. This PR introduces a pluggable constrained-decoding backend interface and implements two backends: a CFG/grammar-anchored backend and a regex-backend with explicit token-aware handling. Key goals were: (1) keep streaming stable and low-latency while enforcing constraints; (2) fix tokenizer-edge cases where constraints span token boundaries; (3) make the OpenAI compatibility layer mapping for the `structured_output` parameter predictable across backend choices; (4) add fuzz and unit tests that exercise complex grammars and regexes. Summary of changes: - Add `constrained_decoder` backend interface (token-level API) to runtime; backends implement `accept`, `is_complete`, and `next_allowed_token_ids` hooks. - Implement `cfg_backend` that compiles user-supplied grammar (PEG/CFG subset) into a deterministic state machine and tracks parse states across partial/streamed tokens. It supports left-recursive patterns via a guarded expansion and exposes descriptive failure reasons for better client errors. - Implement `regex_backend` that compiles regex patterns into a small NFA/DFA and uses tokenizer-aware anchors to avoid splitting matches across tokens; it supports lookaheads by keeping bounded context buffers. - Streaming fixes: decoder now flushes partial token buffers only when safe, emits partial chunks without violating constraints, and performs constraint checks at byte/token boundaries to avoid mid-token failures. - Tokenizer edge-case handling: when a constraint can match across token boundaries, the runtime temporarily buffers sub-token bytes and consults the backend; if backend requires additional bytes, decoder delays emission but continues transfer of streaming frames with a stable prefix token stream. - OpenAI compatibility mapping: the compatibility layer now maps the `structured_output` top-level option into `decoding.backend` plus `backend.options` for grammar/regex parameters; unknown backends return a 400 with actionable text. - API ergonomics: added `backend_hint` to the public API so clients can opt-in to "cfg" or "regex" routing; default remains the legacy behavior (compatibility shim) but is deprecated in 2 releases. - Extensive tests: unit tests for cross-token regex matches, integration tests exercising long streaming sessions, fuzz tests against random grammars to validate safety and failure messaging. - Docs and examples: updated docs/structured-output.md and added a small example in redwood-quickstarts showing a CFG-based form extraction. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves existing decoding when `structured_output` is not provided. When `structured_output` is provided without an explicit `backend`, the compatibility shim attempts to pick the best backend (CFG if grammar-like, regex otherwise) and logs a deprecation warning recommending callers explicitly set the backend. Performance: CFG backend introduces small per-token overhead (microbenchmarked at ~3-5% throughput regression in worst-case pathological grammars) but supports aggressive caching of compiled grammars and state snapshots to reduce runtime costs. The PR contains benchmarks and a recommended caching policy for production use. Merge rationale: provides a modular way to add future backends (JSON-schema style validator, semantic constraints), fixes multiple customer-reported tokenization bugs, and makes the OpenAI compatibility layer deterministic.
commits: feat(constrained-decoder): add backend interface and runtime hooks
feat(cfg-backend): implement grammar-backed constrained decoding and state tracking
feat(regex-backend): implement tokenizer-aware regex backend with lookahead support
fix(streaming): delay partial token flushes when constraints require extra context
test: add unit/integration/fuzz tests for constrained decoding
docs: add structured-output backend docs and compatibility mapping
chore: add bench scripts for backend performance
changed_snippets: runtime/decoder/constrained_decoder.go: added Backend interface with Accept(tokenID string) -> bool and NextAllowedIDs() -> []int helpers
regex_backend.go: tokenizer-aware match loop that consults tokenizer.tokenToByteOffsets to avoid slicing multi-byte tokens
openai_compat/structured_output_adapter.go: map structured_output.{grammar,pattern,backend} -> decoding.backend + backend.options; return 400 for unknown backend
review_comments: Evan Brooks: Can we avoid buffering entire token byte sequences for long-running streams? Suggest adding a bounded sliding window and early-reject heuristics.
Maya Patel (reply): Implemented a bounded context buffer with configurable max_bytes and an early-fail path that returns descriptive errors. Added benchmarks to show memory boundedness.
Sana Iqbal: We should ensure failure messages are actionable for customers. Consider adding error codes and sample remediation in docs.
Maya Patel (reply): Added structured error codes (ERR_CONSTRAINT_MISMATCH, ERR_INCOMPLETE_TOKEN_CONTEXT) and extended docs with remediation steps.
Diego Ramirez: Unit tests flaked on CI for unicode grapheme clusters. Looks like tokenizer->byte mapping mismatch.
Maya Patel (reply): Fixed tokenizer mapping in regex backend and added additional tests for grapheme clusters. Re-ran CI and it passed.
ci_summary: CI: lint ✓, unit tests ✓, integration tests ✓ (flaky test fixed), fuzz run ✓, benchmarks smoke ✓
release_notes: Added pluggable constrained-decoding backends (CFG and regex), fixed tokenizer boundary bugs for structured-output, introduced `backend_hint` and compatibility mappings for the OpenAI layer. Backwards-compatible by default; explicit backend selection recommended.
notes_for_release:
- Admins should enable grammar cache in prod (see docs).
- Update OpenAI compatibility clients to pass `backend_hint` to avoid deprecation warnings.
- Monitor decoder:constrained_backend.* metrics for first week after rollout.
related_incidents: INC-2026-03: customer reported streaming truncation for multi-token regex; fixed by this PR
additional_context: This PR sets up the architecture for future backends (json-schema, semantic validators). The implementation surfaces clear failure reasons to improve customer debugging and aligns the OpenAI compatibility layer semantics with explicit backend selection.
